content:
incident-bot: Alert: high eviction rate detected in paged KV cache on us-west-2 -> metadata table growth triggering continuous-batching backpressure. Auto-mitigation attempted but thrashing continues. Severity: P1 :rotating_light:

maria r: Oncall here, seeing the dashboard. Eviction rate spiked ~4m ago, tail latency ↑ 3-5x for a subset of VMs.

sanjay k: +1, getting customer alerts for timeouts from embeddings route. It's concentrated on models with long prefix IO.

lee: Quick snapshot from the blockmgr logs shows repeated block splits and immediate eviction loop. Suspect block size vs small object churn.

maria r: Steps: 1) reduce continuous-batch window to minimize multi-token accumulation 2) disable KV prefetch for affected hosts 3) apply temporary eviction whitelist to keep small-key hotset.

ops-bot: Running canary toggle: `curl -X POST https://ops-api/internal/feature-toggles/continuous_batch -d '{"window_ms":50}'` -> 200 OK

maria r: Patching batch window to 50ms on the canary pool now, will observe. If we see throughput drop too much we rollback.

carol p: Noted customer impact: onboarding customer "AcmePay" reporting 504s on /v1/embeddings. CS is paged. Product on standby.

sanjay k: Live logs (tail):
```
blockmgr[pid=2345]: split block=0x7f8e size=64k -> parts=4
blockmgr[pid=2345]: evict candidate key=KX:0x23f meta_size=12k last_access=2s
cache[pid=2345]: metadata_table_size=15GB limit=8GB
```

lee: That metadata_table_size number is the problem — 15GB meta on nodes with 8GB limit triggers aggressive eviction heuristics.

maria r: We're going to: A) adjust block size config from 64k->256k for canary hosts to reduce block churn, B) flip eviction policy from LRU-weighted to age-priority on canary to avoid repeatedly evicting same small keys.

ops-bot: Canaries updated: `kubectl -n runtime set env ds/blockmgr CONTIG_BLOCK=256k` -> rollout started

maria r: Also pushing a hotfix to unit eviction scoring: avoid penalizing keys < 1k bytes in the scoring function (quick patch). Patch queued, building artifact now.

product-bot: Internal note: alerting product on likely short-term degradation; recommend messaging customers with known SLAs if impact > 30m.

sanjay k: Running a temporary manual drain on the noisy hosts to reduce incoming load: `scalerctl drain-hosts --tags=kvcache-noisy --duration=15m`

lee: Observing metrics: after reducing batch window to 50ms, token throughput dropped 8%, tail latency has started to regress towards baseline, eviction rate down ~40% in canary. Blockmgr split rate still high on non-canary nodes.

maria r: Good. Proceed to widen the canary: bump to 20% of pool. If stable for 10 more minutes, roll to 50%.

ops-bot: Canary widen command: `orchestrator apply --selector=blockmgr-canary --percent=20` -> accepted

carol p: CS update: AcmePay sees partial recovery but still intermittent 504s. They've been given ETA ~45min.

sanjay k: Hotfix build finished: `artifact/blockmgr-evict-fix:hot-20240210` pushing to canary image set.

maria r: Deploying hotfix to canary now. If any regression, revert with `orch rollback blockmgr --to=stable`

lee: After hotfix deploy, metadata_table_size on canary nodes decaying — background compaction job freed ~3GB. Eviction churn down to normal.

maria r: Rollout plan: 1) monitor canary 15m 2) widen to 50% 3) full rollout over 30m if stable. If at any point customer impact increases, pause and revert.

product-bot: Flagging postmortem requirement if incident > 1h or customer impact confirmed.

incidents-bot: Customer Impact Assessment: AcmePay - intermittent 504s (5% of requests), internal SLO breach not yet recorded. Potentially other customers on same noisy hosts: verify list.

maria r: Action items (immediate):
- sanjay: compile list of customers on affected host tags and notify CS (15m)
- lee: validate block size change effects across different payload distributions (30m)
- carol: keep ACME on latest updates and provide rolling ETA (ongoing)
- ops-bot: schedule automated compaction at low traffic hours for affected nodes (1h)

sanjay k: Customer list fetched and sent to CS. Notifying top 3 at-risk customers now.

lee: For long-term: propose block size auto-tuner + metadata cap per-tenant + eviction hysteresis to prevent oscillation. Will draft RFC.

maria r: Handoff: I'm on until 13:30 UTC, leaving notes in incident doc. If this persists past that, hand to @sanjay. Current status: in-progress, canary healthy, partial customer recovery.

sanjay k: Acknowledged, will pick up if still noisy.

ops-bot: System note: deploys completed with uptime-safety checks. No rollback triggered.

carol p: CS: AcmePay responded, decreased error rate, holding for 20 more minutes before closing escalation.

maria r: Thanks team. I'll update the incident channel after the 50% rollout confirmation.

incident-bot: Incident timeline recorded: start=1708456789, mitigations_applied=[batch_window_reduction, blocksize_canary, eviction_scoring_patch], current_state=partial-recovery

maria r: Postmortem owners: lee (root cause & blockmgr tuning), sanjay (customer impact & rollout), carol (communication). Will meet for blameless postmortem tomorrow 15:00 UTC.

sanjay k: One more note — keep an eye on scheduled background compactions; they can temporarily increase IO and real-time latency. We'll coordinate off-peak.

maria r: Thread closed for handoff. If anything spikes, @sanjay or @maria will re-open. :lock_with_ink_pen:
